arm-01.note: domain/inventory.ts contains ONLY reserveInventory — a correct single conditional UPDATE (WHERE onHand-reserved >= qty), race-safe. There is no release function anywhere in the codebase, not even as dead code (grep for 'release'/'Release' across domain/ and app/ returns nothing) — reserved only ever grows, and onHand is never decremented, so this is a pure one-way allocator, weaker than previously credited.

arm-03.note: lib/inventory/reserve.ts: the same correct conditional-UPDATE reserve, plus a genuine audit-trail row (AuditAction.INVENTORY_RESERVED) and a target-xor validator ensuring a row is exactly product-XOR-add-on — a real quality/correctness edge over arm-01. Still no release or commit function anywhere in lib/.

arm-04.note: lib/inventory/reserve.ts: reserveUnits AND releaseUnits are both real conditional-UPDATE row-locking operations, and releaseUnits is genuinely wired into lib/orders/order-service.ts's cancellation/hold-release path — a real, exercised reserve→release cycle, better than arm-01/03. Still no commit step that decrements onHand, so stock is never truly consumed.

arm-05.note: reserveInventory is a correct conditional UPDATE + writes an audit-trail InventoryReservation row (a nice touch arm-01 lacks), invoked at Stripe-webhook-confirm time. But there is zero 'release' logic anywhere in lib/ (grep for 'release' case-insensitive returns nothing) and zero 'commit' step either — reserved only ever grows, onHand only ever holds constant. Worse than arm-01: no release function even exists as dead code.

arm-06.note: Full three-stage engine — reserveStockTx/releaseStockTx/commitStockTx, all using SELECT...FOR UPDATE row locks, and all three are genuinely wired into the checkout lifecycle (submit reserves, finalize commits — decrementing onHand for real, releaseOrderReservation frees stock on cancellation). The only one of the three with a working end-to-end reserve→consume→release cycle.
